title: Redwood enterprise procedures kit — company operations (2026)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document centralizes company-wide operational policies and ready-to-use process templates covering access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. It is intended as the canonical reference for operational owners, approvers, and team leads.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and suppliers who request access, make changes to production systems, handle company data, engage vendors, or incur business travel/expenses. Exceptions must be approved by the owner_team (finance-legal) and recorded in the exceptions register.

Principles
- Least privilege and auditable approvals for access.
- Risk-proportional controls: higher risk => higher review/fail-safe.
- Single source of truth for templates to speed approvals and audits.
- Clear ownership for every control and handoff.

Owners and escalation
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner: Maya Chen).
- Operational owners: People Ops (travel & people-related expenses), Eng-SRE (change management for infra), Eng-Platform (deployment change policies), Procurement (vendor onboarding), Security (data classification & RBAC design).
- Escalation channel: #ops-escalation (Slack); for regulatory incidents notify security@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com.

1) Access & Permissions
Summary: RBAC-based model with centralized requests through the Access Request Portal (ARP). Temporary elevation via Just-In-Time (JIT) access is encouraged.
Responsibilities:
- Requester: provide justification and duration.
- Approver: manager or service owner depending on resource type.
- IAM admin: perform provisioning and maintain audit logs.

Access categories and approval matrix (summary):
| Resource type | Approver | Max default duration | Escalation threshold |
|---------------|----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| Non-prod cloud project | Team manager | 90 days | Security review if > 30 days or cross-team |
| Prod read-only role | Service owner | 30 days | Security review if > 30 days |
| Prod write / admin role | Service owner + Security | 7 days | Required approval from Eng-SRE for > 7 days |
| Vendor access (limited) | Procurement + Service owner | 14 days | Contract/DPAs required for > 30 days |

Request process (high level):
1. Submit ARP form including business justification, requested resources, and duration.
2. Auto-notify approver(s); if multi-approver, require all approvals.
3. IAM admin provisions account/role and tags request id for audit.
4. Access automatically expires at the requested end date; reminders sent 7 days before expiry.

Temporary elevation/JIT steps:
1. Request JIT via ARP with short justification and immediate timeline.
2. Approver reviews and sets a task window; JIT sessions are logged and session recordings retained for 90 days.

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly reviews for all active Prod admin roles.
- Annual certification for vendor accounts.

2) Change Management
Goal: enable fast, safe, and auditable changes across infra and product services.
Change categories:
- Standard change: pre-authorized, repeatable operational tasks (e.g., routine scaling) — no CAB required but must follow runbook.
- Normal change: requires change ticket, impact assessment, approver sign-off, and scheduled window.
- Emergency change: implemented to remediate incidents. Post-implementation review required within 72 hours.

Change request template (short):
- Title
- Owner/Requester
- Change category (standard/normal/emergency)
- Impact assessment (services/users, rollback plan)
- Scheduled window
- Validation plan / smoke tests

Approval matrix:
- Normal change: Service owner + Eng-SRE (for infra) or Product owner (for API) depending on impact.
- High-impact (customer-facing outage risk): CAB approval required. CAB meets twice weekly; use asynchronous voting for low-latency approvals.

Implementation steps (normal change):
1. Open change ticket in Change Management system (link: /tools/change).
2. Fill template, attach runbook, assign approvers.
3. Complete pre-change checklist (backups, canary, synthetic checks).
4. Execute in maintenance window.
5. Run validation tests.
6. Close ticket with outcomes and metrics (latency, error rate).

Emergency change protocol:
1. Tag ticket as EMERGENCY; notify on-call and #incident.
2. Implement mitigation with minimum scope.
3. After stabilization, conduct a post-implementation review within 72 hours.

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Production major releases blocked on high-traffic holidays (list maintained by Product).
- Routine changes allowed in designated windows: Mon–Fri 02:00–06:00 UTC and Sat 08:00–12:00 UTC (exceptions handled by CAB).

3) Data Management
Classification scheme (three levels):
- PUBLIC: no restrictions.
- INTERNAL: default for business documents.
- RESTRICTED: PII, customer data, proprietary model weights.

Data handling requirements:
- RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest and in transit, stored in approved buckets, and access controlled via RBAC with explicit justification.
- Export/egress of RESTRICTED data requires a Data Use Request and DSA review (Data Security & Assurance).

Retention and deletion
- Logs (diagnostic): 180 days by default, extendable to 365 days upon SRE request.
- Backups: retention per service SLA; restore tests quarterly.
- Customer data retention: as per contract or 7 years max unless otherwise specified.

Data breach steps (summary):
1. Contain and preserve evidence.
2. Notify Security and Legal within 24 hours.
3. Conduct forensics; follow regulatory notification timelines.

Data labeling and metadata requirements:
- Every dataset must include: owner, classification, retention policy, last updated, and approved uses.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement lifecycle:
1. Need identification and owner assignment.
2. Create Purchase Request (PR) using Procurement template (see Templates section).
3. Competitive sourcing required for purchases > $50k.
4. Procurement team reviews vendor compliance (security, SOC2, DPAs) and negotiates terms.
5. Purchase Order (PO) issued; vendor onboarding completed.

Approval thresholds (summary):
- Up to $2,500: Team lead approval.
- $2,500–$50,000: Department head + Procurement review.
- > $50,000: VP approval + Procurement + Legal.

Card and travel expenses:
- Use corporate card for approved travel with pre-approval.
- Expense report due within 14 days of trip end.
- Receipts required for any individual expense > $25.
- Per diem model: US domestic $75/day (meals & incidental), international vary by country — check Finance portal.

Reimbursements and audit
- Finance reserves the right to audit expense claims for 12 months.
- Non-compliant claims will be remediated with manager and may lead to revocation of card privileges.

Procurement request example (JSON snippet to paste into PR form):
```
{
  "requester": "Name",
  "department": "Engineering",
  "description": "GPU cloud capacity: 4 x A100 reserved for Q1 experiments",
  "estimated_cost": "48,000",
  "vendor": "CloudCompute Inc.",
  "business_justification": "Prototype + evaluation for Dedicated offering",
  "approval_chain": ["team-lead", "procurement"]
}
```

5) Vendor Management
Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Complete vendor intake form and risk assessment.
2. Verify security posture (SOC 2, ISO, pen-test results if applicable).
3. Data processing addendum (DPA) and contractual terms signed by Legal.
4. Create vendor record in Vendor Registry with owner and contract dates.
5. Provision necessary access and limit by least privilege.

SLAs and monitoring:
- Key vendors must have a documented SLA and escalations.
- Quarterly vendor review for strategic vendors; annual review for others.

Offboarding:
- Revoke all accounts and access within 48 hours of contract termination.
- Verify data return/destruction per contract.

6) Travel Policy (summary)
Pre-approval: All business travel requires a Travel Request in the Travel Portal and manager pre-approval.
Booking: Use preferred travel vendors for corporate rates; personal arrangements reimbursable only with prior approval.
Safety & compliance: Follow local guidance and travel advisories; register high-risk travel with People Ops.
Expense categories and caps:
- Lodging: reasonable nightly rate per city band (see Finance portal).
- Meals: per diem or itemized receipts.
- Ground transport: ride-share or economy car rental.

Travel emergency support: 24/7 travel assistance is available via travel-support@redwood.com.

7) Internal Templates (canonical templates to use)
- Access Request (ARP) template (fields: requester, resource, duration, justification, approver).
- Change Request template (fields: owner, impact, rollback, validation, stakeholders).
- Procurement Request (PR) template (fields: requester, vendor, cost, justification, approvals).
- Vendor Intake form (fields: vendor, controls checklist, contracts, risk rating).
- Travel Request template (fields: traveler, dates, destination, business purpose, manager approval).

Example Access Request (text):
--Start ARP--
Requester: Jane Doe
Resource: prod-ml-models S3 bucket (RESTRICTED)
Duration: 7 days
Justification: Investigate model drift for customer incident #1234
Approver: Service owner (ML Infra), Security (if > 3 days)
--End ARP--

Governance and audit
- All actions (access grants, change tickets, procurement approvals) must be tagged with policy id and retained per retention rules.
- Internal audit cadence: semi-annual for access controls, quarterly for change management evidence, annual for procurement/vendor compliance.

Amendments and exceptions
- To request an exception, submit an Exception Request with rationale, compensating controls, and expiration date. Exceptions expire automatically unless renewed via the same process.

FAQs (short)
Q: Who signs off on vendor DPAs?
A: Legal in coordination with Procurement.
Q: How long are access request logs retained?
A: 365 days for provisioning logs; session recordings for 90 days.
